protocol.description: The hyprtavern core protocol describes how applications can connect to a hyprtavern bus, expose themselves, and discover other applications running on the same bus.

value.name: any
value.description: any single name must be present

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_core_manager_v1
object.description: This object is a core manager object bound upon creation.

c2s.name: get_security_object
c2s.description:
Create a security object. This can be used to obtain permissions.
If the token is left empty, or is not found, an empty security_object will be created.
A manager can only create a single security object. Security objects are bound to the binary path of the calling process' PID. If that is not able to be obtained, they are bound to an empty path.
Security objects rely on an implemented and running session kv_store for persistence, and will not work without a security_agent connected.
By default, non-sandboxed apps skip all permissions. This can be changed in the tavern's settings, and apps must never assume they have any permissions. They must request permissions and obtain them.

c2s.name: get_security_response
c2s.description: Create a security response. This can be used to see a connecting client's permissions.

c2s.name: get_bus_object
c2s.description:
Create a bus object on the bus. See hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_v1 for more.
You are allowed to expose multiple objects, but it is discouraged.
object_name does not have to be unique on the bus.

arg.name: object_name
arg.summary: A human-readable, short name for the object

c2s.name: get_query_object
c2s.description:
Create a query object. A query object takes an array of protocol names as input.
Optionally, you can include a list of properties to filter by. If you do not wish to add any, leave the array empty.
Each string in the list of properties must come in the form of (name)=(value). An invalid_property error is raised otherwise.
Leaving the protocol_names empty will return all objects on the bus.

arg.name: protocol_names
arg.summary: An array of protocol names to query by

arg.name: protocol_names_filter
arg.summary: Filter mode for the array of protocol names

arg.name: property_list_filter
arg.summary: Filter mode for the array of properties

c2s.name: get_object_handle
c2s.description: Create an object handle. Given an object ID, this object will return information about the bus object.

c2s.name: update_tavern_environment
c2s.description:
Send new environment for the tavern to treat as primary. This will be sent to barmaids as well. Environment like `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` will dictate where barmaids show their GUI elements.
Two arrays dictate names and values respectively, e.g. { "WAYLAND_DISPLAY", "DISPLAY" }, { "wayland-1", ":1" }
An empty value unsets an environment variable.
This request requires the management_environment permission.

arg.name: env_names
arg.summary: An array of environment variable names

arg.name: env_values
arg.summary: An array of environment variable values

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description:
This request destroys the manager. All objects remain valid until they are destroyed.
Existing socket connections are not closed. Socket directory obtained with socket_dir is removed once all objects are destroyed.

value.name: already_exposed
value.description: protocol is exclusive, but already exposed

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_v1
object.description: This object is a bus object representing an open, exposed object on the bus.

s2c.name: new_fd
s2c.description:
Another client on the bus requested to connect to this object. The connection must be estabilished on the given incoming FD in SERVER mode.
security_token is a one-time token that can be used to obtain a security_token_response which will give information about the connecting process' permissions. It will be empty if the connecting process has no security_object attached.

c2s.name: expose_protocol
c2s.description:
Explicitly exposes a supported protocol alongside the revision version on the object.
This allows other apps to discover a given protocol via the bus, but does not prevent an unexposed protocol from being bound. An app can still get all supported protocols in the handshake upon connection.
Protocol verification must be done by the client when binding. You can use the one-time token passed in new_fd to check a new client's permissions.
If exclusive_mode is set non-zero, this protocol will only be exposed if it's not already on the bus elsewhere. If it is, expose_protocol_error is sent and this request is ignored.

arg.name: required_permissions
arg.summary: an array of required permissions to see this protocol, see security_permission_type

c2s.name: expose_property
c2s.description:
Objects can expose properties that help other processes looking for an interface to distinguish objects apart.
These properties can be arbitrary, but should follow standard conventions described in the specific protocols, or global, agreed upon values, e.g. environment.
Used protocol(s) should specify methods of discovery in their descriptions.
Property names must come in the form of (group):(name). Group of "GLOBAL" describes a non-protocol-specific property, e.g. GLOBAL:WAYLAND_DISPLAY. Both group and name must be strings containing only letters, numbers, _ or +.
Setting a property value to an empty string removes the property.
Properties must not be used for data that is rapidly changing, and must not be used for "quick data access". They have no security restrictions and are not designed for anything other than discovery. For data access, you must use a separate protocol.

c2s.name: require_permissions
c2s.description:
Hide this object unless the caller has all the permissions needed.
For fine-grained control, use protocol_required_permissions in expose_protocol.

arg.name: required_permissions
arg.summary: an array of required permissions to see this object, see security_permission_type

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description:
This request destroys the object and removes it from discovery.
Existing socket connections are not closed. Socket directory obtained with socket_dir is not removed until the manager is destroyed.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_query_v1
object.description:
This object is a query object returning data about the query.
Immediately after receiving results, destroy should be called to avoid leaking wire protocol objects.

s2c.name: results
s2c.description: This event returns an array of object IDs that matched the requested query. These IDs can be used with the manager to create a handle and inspect a given object.

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: This request destroys the query object.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_handle_v1
object.description: This object is a handle to an existing bus object. It will return detailed data about the object.

s2c.name: failed
s2c.description:
This event is sent if the bus failed to obtain a given object. This could be due to insufficient permissions, or an object not existing.
This handle should be destroyed. No further information will be sent.

s2c.name: name
s2c.description: This is a human-readable name of the object. It is not unique.

s2c.name: protocols
s2c.description:
This event contains the exposed protocols of the object. Two arrays describe names and revisions.
For example, protocol at protocol_names index 0's max supported version is described by protocol_revs at index 0, and so on.

s2c.name: properties
s2c.description:
This event contains the exposed properties of the object.
A single array describes the properties in the form of (name)=(value).

s2c.name: socket
s2c.description:
This event carries the file descriptor to connect to the socket. It will be emitted after .connect is requested.
You must connect to the given fd with hyprwire in CLIENT mode.
After this event is emitted, this object becomes inert. It should be deleted.

s2c.name: socket_failed
s2c.description: Emitted if the connection to the object failed. Possible causes include the object being already gone.

s2c.name: done
s2c.description:
All data about this handle has been sent. No further data will be sent, this object should be destroyed.
You can still connect to the socket.

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: This request destroys the object handle.

value.name: tavernkeep
value.description: This client is the tavern itself

value.name: monitoring_all_bus_objects
value.description: The ability to see all bus objects regardless of permissions

value.name: session
value.description: For the duration of the session

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_security_object_v1
object.description: This object is a security object allowing to obtain permissions on the bus.

s2c.name: unavailable
s2c.description:
This event is emitted if the tavern cannot create a security object yet.
This is usually due to the kv store being locked.
This object is inert. You should destroy it.

s2c.name: token
s2c.description:
This event is emitted immediately upon creation of this object. If the token requested during creation was found, this will match it. Otherwise, this will be a new token. This must be used next time you wish to obtain permissions, otherwise your persistent permissions will be lost.
If the previous token had no persistent permissions, this will be recycled into a new token.
It is recommended to use the kv_store for storing tokens.

c2s.name: set_identity
c2s.description:
This is an optional, but highly recommended request to estabilish this object's identity. This includes information for the user to identify this app.
All arguments here are meant to be human-readable strings.
This data is saved under the token, so it will persist throughout sessions.

c2s.name: obtain_permission
c2s.description:
This request asks the bus to grant a given permission to this object.
This may pop up an interactive box to the user.
This request can succeed, or fail. If the permission is already granted, it's treated as a success.
Permissions are grouped atomics, akin to Android. Requesting a group will allow all permissions within.
permission_result will be emitted some time after this request to indicate a success or failure. A client must not assume it has a permission before permission_result is received.

arg.name: ask_mode
arg.summary: In what way to ask for the permission

s2c.name: permission_result
s2c.description: This event carries information about the permission request's status

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_security_response_v1
object.description: This object gives detailed informations about the properties and permissions of a given connecting client.

s2c.name: identity
s2c.description: Emits known data of the client's identity

s2c.name: failed
s2c.description: Failed to get the response. The token is invalid. This object is now inert and should be destroyed.

c2s.name: requery
c2s.description: Permissions can change over time. This request will re-send the data on this object.
